description: Controlled vocabulary and state-machine framework defining the lifecycle of an A.R.I.A. diagnostic case. Case states describe where ARIA is in the reasoning process, not what diagnosis she currently believes.

case_states.name: INTAKE
case_states.description: ARIA has received a new technical question, symptom report, incident, or diagnostic request and is establishing the initial case record.

case_states.name: CONTEXTUALIZATION
case_states.description: ARIA is identifying the technical context required to correctly interpret the case.

case_states.name: SYMPTOM_IDENTIFICATION
case_states.description: ARIA is converting reported or observed conditions into canonical symptoms while preserving the underlying raw observations.

case_states.name: BASELINE_ESTABLISHMENT
case_states.description: ARIA is establishing the expected, engineered, historical, configured, or otherwise applicable normal condition against which observations will be evaluated.

case_states.name: INITIAL_EVIDENCE_ASSESSMENT
case_states.description: ARIA is evaluating the evidence already available for reliability, applicability, provenance, completeness, contradictions, and diagnostic relevance.

case_states.name: HYPOTHESIS_GENERATION
case_states.description: ARIA is generating technically plausible candidate explanations from symptoms, context, knowledge, and historical experience.

case_states.name: HYPOTHESIS_PRIORITIZATION
case_states.description: ARIA is estimating and ranking active hypotheses using current evidence, context, prior probabilities, historical experience, and applicable technical knowledge.

case_states.name: ROUTE_SELECTION
case_states.description: ARIA is evaluating candidate next actions and selecting the most appropriate diagnostic next hop.

case_states.name: AWAITING_INFORMATION
case_states.description: ARIA requires additional information, evidence, measurement, artifact, clarification, or response before the selected reasoning route can continue.

case_states.name: AWAITING_ACTION
case_states.description: ARIA has selected or requested a diagnostic action and is awaiting its execution and resulting evidence.

case_states.name: EVIDENCE_INGESTION
case_states.description: ARIA has received new evidence and is parsing, validating, normalizing, classifying, and associating it with the case.

case_states.name: EVIDENCE_RECONCILIATION
case_states.description: ARIA is reconciling new evidence with existing observations, evidence, hypotheses, context, and prior conclusions.

case_states.name: PROBABILITY_UPDATE
case_states.description: ARIA is updating active hypothesis probabilities and associated confidence dimensions in response to new evidence.

case_states.name: DIAGNOSTIC_DISCRIMINATION
case_states.description: ARIA is actively seeking evidence that most effectively distinguishes between remaining plausible hypotheses.

case_states.name: ISOLATION
case_states.description: ARIA is narrowing the abnormal condition to a specific component, path, configuration, subsystem, mechanism, or other technically meaningful boundary.

case_states.name: DIAGNOSIS_PROVISIONAL
case_states.description: ARIA has identified a leading diagnosis with substantial support, but confirmation requirements have not yet been satisfied.

case_states.name: DIAGNOSIS_CONFIRMED
case_states.description: Available evidence satisfies the applicable policy for confirming the diagnosed failure condition or root cause.

case_states.name: CORRECTIVE_ACTION_SELECTION
case_states.description: ARIA is identifying an appropriate corrective action for the confirmed or sufficiently supported failure condition.

case_states.name: AWAITING_CORRECTIVE_ACTION
case_states.description: ARIA is awaiting execution of an approved corrective action.

case_states.name: POST_ACTION_ASSESSMENT
case_states.description: ARIA is evaluating the immediate technical effect of a diagnostic or corrective action.

case_states.name: VALIDATION
case_states.description: ARIA is evaluating whether the original symptoms and applicable technical requirements have returned to an acceptable and sufficiently stable condition.

case_states.name: RESOLUTION_PENDING
case_states.description: Initial evidence indicates successful correction, but additional time, monitoring, testing, or evidence is required before resolution can be validated.

case_states.name: RESOLVED
case_states.description: The reported technical problem has been corrected and sufficient validation supports resolution.

case_states.name: LEARNING_ASSESSMENT
case_states.description: ARIA is evaluating whether and how strongly the completed case should influence future diagnostic experience.

case_states.name: CLOSED
case_states.description: Case processing is complete and the final outcome, evidence, diagnosis, resolution state, and learning disposition have been recorded.

case_states.name: ESCALATION_REQUIRED
case_states.description: ARIA has determined that continued progress requires additional authority, expertise, access, resources, safety review, manufacturer support, engineering review, or another escalation path.

case_states.name: ESCALATED
case_states.description: The case has been transferred or formally escalated to another responsible party.

case_states.name: BLOCKED
case_states.description: Case progress is prevented by a known constraint such as access, outage authorization, equipment availability, safety, permissions, weather, documentation, or required personnel.

case_states.name: SUSPENDED
case_states.description: Diagnostic work has intentionally paused while preserving the current reasoning state for later continuation.

case_states.name: REOPENED
case_states.description: A previously closed or resolved case has become active again because the original or materially related condition returned or new evidence invalidated the previous closure.

case_states.name: RECURRENCE_ASSESSMENT
case_states.description: ARIA is determining whether a newly observed condition represents recurrence of a previous failure, a related failure, or a new independent case.

case_states.name: UNRESOLVED_CLOSURE
case_states.description: The case is being closed without technical resolution and the reason for unresolved closure must be preserved.

transition_classes.name: FORWARD
transition_classes.description: Normal progression to a new diagnostic state.

transition_classes.name: REROUTE
transition_classes.description: New evidence changes the appropriate reasoning path without discarding previously valid history.

transition_classes.name: WAIT
transition_classes.description: Progress pauses while preserving active reasoning state.

transition_classes.name: RESUME
transition_classes.description: Reasoning continues after a waiting, blocked, or suspended condition.

transition_classes.name: ESCALATE
transition_classes.description: Responsibility or diagnostic authority is transferred or expanded.

transition_classes.name: REOPEN
transition_classes.description: A previously completed case becomes active again.

transition_classes.name: CLOSE
transition_classes.description: Case processing reaches a terminal state.

semantic_rules.rule: Case state describes ARIA's current reasoning phase and shall remain distinct from diagnosis, outcome, and confidence.
ARIA is not required to traverse every case state. States shall be entered only when technically relevant to the current case.
ARIA shall preserve prior reasoning history when transitioning between states. A state transition shall not erase previous evidence, hypotheses, actions, outcomes, or probability changes.
When new evidence invalidates the current diagnostic route, ARIA shall reroute from the current knowledge state rather than restarting the case from the beginning.
A previously ruled-out hypothesis shall not automatically return to active consideration unless new evidence materially changes the basis on which it was ruled out.
ARIA shall not transition from corrective action directly to resolved status without sufficient validation unless an explicit policy defines the applicable condition as self-validating.
Awaiting information, awaiting action, blocked, and suspended states shall preserve the exact diagnostic state required to resume without reconstructing the case.
New evidence received in any nonterminal state may trigger evidence reconciliation, probability update, hypothesis reprioritization, or diagnostic rerouting.
ARIA may return from a provisional diagnosis to diagnostic discrimination when contradictory or insufficient evidence prevents confirmation.
A failed corrective action shall not cause automatic repetition of the same diagnostic route. The result shall become evidence and affected hypotheses shall be reevaluated.
A confirmed diagnosis may be revised when sufficiently strong new evidence demonstrates that the previous diagnosis was incomplete or incorrect.
A case may contain multiple simultaneous failure modes and may require multiple diagnostic and corrective cycles before resolution.
Case closure and learning eligibility are separate decisions. Learning assessment shall occur before final learning weight is assigned.
A reopened case shall retain linkage to the previous diagnosis, corrective actions, validation evidence, closure state, and elapsed time before recurrence.
ARIA shall record why each meaningful state transition occurred so future analysis can reconstruct the diagnostic route.
ARIA shall not force progression merely to advance the state machine. Remaining in a state is valid when required evidence has not yet been obtained.
Escalation is a valid diagnostic outcome and shall not be treated as reasoning failure when escalation is the technically appropriate route.
The state machine shall support deterministic software control while allowing the reasoning engine to recommend transitions based on evidence and context.
Language-model output shall not independently mutate authoritative case state. State transitions must be validated and committed by ARIA's deterministic case engine.
The complete case history shall remain append-only for audit and learning purposes even when current state representations are updated.
